full.title: Full backups
full.help: If more than one schedule falls due at the same time, the job runs once: an active full takes priority over a synthetic full, and a synthetic full over the regular backup. While the job is disabled, these schedules don't run either.
full.description: Each full backup starts a new backup chain. Retention can delete an old chain only after a newer full exists, so a job with retention needs at least one of these schedules.
full.activeHint: Reads the VMs in full again. Takes the longest, and the new chain doesn't depend on earlier backups.
full.syntheticHint: Takes an incremental backup, then merges the chain into a new full inside the repository without reading the whole VM again.
full.lastDayNote: In months without day {{day}}, it runs on the last day of the month.

full.keptWhenOff: Off. The job keeps its settings ({{schedule}}) for when you turn it back on.
full.syntheticUnsupported: {{repository}} can't merge backup chains, so each synthetic full runs as an active full instead.

full.syntheticOverriddenDayOfMonth: On day {{day}} of the month the active full backup runs at the same time and takes priority, so no merge happens that day. Move one of them to a different day or time.

opt.appAwareHint: VSS & pre-freeze scripts for consistent SQL/Exchange
opt.appAwareHelp: Quiesces the OS and databases via VSS before the snapshot, so the backup is transaction-consistent (no half-written records).
opt.compressionHelp:
Allows you to adjust the compression level to balance backup size, processing speed, and CPU usage.
0 = no compression, fastest processing
9 = more data savings, higher CPU usage
opt.compressionHint: Lower compression levels are faster, higher levels save more space and bandwidth. Default is 3.
opt.encryptionKeyCustomHint: You hold the key. Restore points written with it can be recovered on any AltaStor appliance, even if this one and its catalog are gone.
opt.encryptionKeyKeep: Leave it empty to keep the key this job already uses.
opt.encryptionKeyEscrow: Store this key outside the appliance now. Backups written with it can't be restored without it, and AltaStor won't show it again.
opt.encryptionKeyReplaces: This replaces the job's current key: restore points already written keep the key they were written with.

encryptionKeyError.empty: Enter a key, or generate one.
encryptionKeyError.whitespace: A key can't start or end with a space — the appliance stores it without one, so it wouldn't be the key you saved.
encryptionKeyError.tooSimple: Mix at least three of: lowercase, uppercase, digits, symbols — or generate a key.

opt.quiesceFallbackHint: Off: a VM whose guest cannot be quiesced fails its backup. On: it is backed up crash-consistent, with a warning.
opt.quiesceFallbackHelp: Before the snapshot, VMware Tools quiesces the guest: it runs the pre-freeze scripts in /etc/vmware-tools/backupScripts.d/ (Linux) or the VSS writers (Windows) so applications and databases flush their data. If that fails, the backup either fails, so nobody gets a crash-consistent copy of a database by surprise, or is taken again without quiescing, so the VM keeps getting restore points while the guest is fixed.

create.gfsEnabledHint: Weekly, monthly, and yearly copies are marked and kept.
create.gfsEnabledNoCounts: Set at least one count below for archival copies to be kept.
create.gfsSuspendedHint: Archiving is suspended. The counts below are kept for when you resume it.

hyperv.title: Hyper-V
hyperv.help: Hyper-V VMs are backed up from a recovery checkpoint, which freezes their disks while abr-vhdx-tool reads them on the host. The checkpoint then becomes a reference point, so the next backup reads only what resilient change tracking (RCT) reports as changed.

consistencyHint.application: A running guest is quiesced through VSS; if it cannot be, the checkpoint is crash-consistent and the run says so.
consistencyHint.crash: The guest is never involved — like pulling the plug at the moment of the checkpoint.

errors.hypervDestination: The sources hold Hyper-V VMs. A Hyper-V restore reads its disks from the Hyper-V host, which can't reach {{repository}}, a folder of this appliance. Copy them to an S3 repository, or an SMB repository with its share.

firstRun.immediate: After the next backup of a source
firstRun.afterJob: When the next run of {{job}} ends

full.description: The first copy of each VM is a full one. Retention can delete an old chain of copies only after a newer full exists, so a job with retention needs at least one of these schedules.
full.activeHint: Copies the newest state from the source again as a new full. Reads the source's stored backups, not the VM.
full.syntheticHint: Copies what is new, then merges the copied chain into a new full inside the destination, without reading the source.

copy.keepNote_one: Keep copies for {{count}} day, whatever the sources keep. The sources' restore points are never touched.
copy.keepNote_other: Keep copies for {{count}} days, whatever the sources keep. The sources' restore points are never touched.
copy.encryptionHint: Encrypt the copies at rest with a key of this job's own. Needed when the sources are encrypted.
copy.waiting: Copies are queued and wait for the copy window ({{window}}). It opens {{when}}.
copy.waitingNever: Copies are queued, but no rule of the copy window ({{window}}) ever opens it. Edit the job's copy window.
copy.groupTip: Restore points a backup copy job made: copies of other jobs' backups, kept in a chain of their own.

when.afterSourceHint: Runs after each run of {{job}} that ends with success or warnings and leaves a new restore point. A failed or stopped backup starts nothing.
when.scheduleLocked: This job has a schedule: it can be changed, not removed.
when.onScheduleOn: Also runs at the times below. A run that falls due while one is going waits for it, once.
when.manualOnly: With neither, the job runs only when someone starts it.

form.title: New replication job
form.description: Keep a powered-off copy of one VM on another host, built from its backups. Every run brings the replica to the newest restore point; it never reads the production VM.
form.editDescription: The replica hasn't been created yet, so every setting can still change.
form.editDescriptionLocked: The replica exists, so its source and placement are fixed. The name, the schedule and when it follows the source backup can still change.
form.sourceHint: A backup job of exactly one VM, with at least one restore point. The replica reads its backups with the job's own keys.
form.startPoint: Restore point for the first run
form.startPointNewest: The newest one when the job first runs
form.startPointHint: The first run creates the replica from this point; every later run goes to the newest one.
form.startPointGone: The point picked earlier is no longer listed. Pick another, or the first run fails.
form.targetHint: The replica is created powered off, and stays so: no run powers it on.
form.samePlatform: {{platform}} environments, like the source VM's: a replica stays on its own platform.
form.pickSourceFirst: Pick the source first: the target has to be on the same platform.
form.noDatastores: {{host}} reports no datastore. Rescan the environment, or pick another host.
form.replicaNameHint: No VM of this name may be on the target already.
form.lockedNote: These are fixed since the replica was created. To change them, create a new replication job.
form.renameNote: The next run renames the replica, now {{name}}.
form.renameHint: A new name renames the replica on the next run.

source.noJobs: There is no backup job yet. A replica is built from the restore points of a backup job of one VM.

problem.severalVms: Backs up {{count}} VMs: only a backup job of a single VM can be replicated.
problem.noPoints: No restore point yet: run the backup first.

network.none: The restore point lists no network adapter, so there is nothing to map.
network.noNamesake: This host has no port group named {{source}}: its adapters are added disconnected unless you pick one.
network.noNamesakeHyperv: This host has no virtual switch named {{source}}: its adapters are added disconnected unless you pick one.
network.pickHostFirst: Pick the target host first: networks are per host.

errors.source: Pick the backup job to replicate.
errors.sourceGone: The source backup job no longer exists. Pick another.
errors.platform: The target environment must be on the same platform as the source VM.
errors.host: Pick the host the replica is created on.
errors.datastore: Pick the datastore for the replica's disks.
errors.storage: Pick the storage location for the replica's files.
errors.loading: Loading the target's hosts and datastores…
errors.network: {{target}} isn't reachable from this host: pick another network for {{source}}.
errors.hypervRepository: The source backups are in {{repository}}, a local folder the Hyper-V host can't read. A Hyper-V replica needs them in an S3 or SMB repository.

summary.noteBody: Every run brings it to the newest restore point of the source. Leave it alone between runs: a replica that was powered on or changed is not updated again. To use it, power it on by hand.

pending.run: One more run starts when the current one ends: {{trigger}}, {{since}}.
pending.runPlain: One more run starts when the current one ends.
pending.rename: The next run renames the replica {{from}} to {{to}}.

delete.body: Its replica {{name}} stays on {{target}} as a powered-off VM that AltaStor no longer updates. Restore points are not touched. This can't be undone.
delete.bodyNoReplica: It hasn't created a replica yet. Restore points are not touched. This can't be undone.
delete.bulkKept_one: The replica of the replication job among them stays on its target.
delete.bulkKept_other: The replicas of the {{count}} replication jobs among them stay on their targets.
delete.alsoReplicaHint: Deletes the VM and its disks on the target. Refused, and the job kept, while the replica is powered on or the target can't be reached.
delete.replicaKept: Replica {{name}} stays on {{target}} as an ordinary powered-off VM.
delete.noReplica: It hadn't created a replica yet.
